answer: Coordination-Delay Pricing: each agent identity gets a verification slot whose release time is set by a hash puzzle calibrated to current network load, like water finding its level down a river. To act in a round, an identity must wait out its slot; parallel identities don't shorten the wait. Attackers pay in elapsed time and idle copper per fake identity, while a gale of sybils still resolves no faster than one honest slot. Cost: sustained latency and hardware occupancy scaling linearly with identity count.
